inputs.text: Angus Taylor has made clear that the Liberals are not ready to challenge the tax advantages enjoyed by gas companies and property investors, shutting down Andrew Hastie’s call to consider reform. This is more than a leadership tussle: it shows how firmly the party protects powerful commercial interests, even as some MPs contemplate a new leadership conversation. Taylor also refused to say whether he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran and did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump. For all the talk of competing philosophies, the public is left with a party unwilling to confront entrenched wealth or speak plainly about the use of military force.
